reason: The continuation gate gained against the 90 modern and switching opponents while its weakest-five score fell against both older development fields. Measure which expert wins identical old positions and fit the same selector with both generations of opponents present.
groups: Before further evaluation freeze three separate development leagues: 90 modern fixed and switching bots, 85 older movement configurations, and 65 additional historical configurations dominated by Zest. The four reserved switch styles and independent human identities remain outside training and selection. Keep each opponent and every input clock visible in the results.
training: Two rounds using the 16 training donors, both seats, both 0 and 80 ms RTTs, the integer virtual mouse and the same five random time bands and four complete-state continuations as the previous experiment. Round one starts from continuation-03 and uses every fighter in the three groups. Round two also includes the first new entrant among the modern opponents and trains on the accumulated examples from both rounds. Ridge loss gives each group one third of the weight and each opponent equal weight within its own group. Initial populations and explicit tables remain frozen.
selection: Compare 27 fitted gates on a fixed stratified half of the training donors, then advance the best four by joint merit alongside W-tap, Hold-W, population, lookup table, previous adaptive, continuation-03 and all earlier new entries. Run the title tournament on all eight exposed development calendars. Compute each group's merit from the equally weighted mean, weakest-five and single weakest opponent. Overall merit is half the lowest group merit plus half the mean of the three group merits. Break ties by mean across groups, then alias. Publish the actual winner and best new controller every round, even if W-tap or an existing contender wins.
transfer: Freeze the top new entrant before prospective validation and before drawing its own eight independent native W-tap mirror clocks. Use its weakest exposed opponent in each group plus W-tap, Hold-W and one reserved switcher (shift-sealed-04), deduplicated. Compare W-tap, the incumbent population fighter, continuation-03 and the newly fitted challenger over both seats, both RTTs and two native repeats. Keep per-opponent, clock, and latency results, with a permanent native tournament winner. This supplementary panel does not change the historical title criteria.
